concerns: The spec (dispatch://LEGION-12/spec v4) assumes the hook multiplies (three candidate causes). Measurement on two live sessions — this planner (headless rpc phase worker, plugin 1.3.0) and the LEGION-16 controller (TUI, PR #961 code, real rig daemon) — plus the host's dispatch code falsifies all three and the 'host invokes the hook N times' variant: see `rootCause.structuralProof` and `rootCause.evidence`. The architect has the deltas in `specDeviations`; the plan follows the measurement, as the spec's Design section says it must, and task 1 re-measures with the instrumented hook so the implementer confirms before changing code.

The spec's stand-in rule 'returns 403 on a reused credential exactly as the real daemon' is wrong about the real daemon: `AuthState.resolveGrant` (packages/daemon/src/daemon/api/auth.ts:119-124) only checks existence and a 60-second expiry (`GRANT_TTL_MS`, api.ts:47); it never consumes a grant. The stand-in must mirror that rule (unknown or expired -> 403; a known live grant redeems any number of times), or it will 403 the real daemon's legitimate re-redemption inside `handleGitCredential` (credentials.ts:50-52 resolves the same grant twice on purpose).

`legion gh -- api user` (spec Testing row for acceptance 3) cannot succeed with a GitHub App installation token even on the real rig: `GET /user` is a user-token endpoint. The rig proves the `legion gh` grant path with `legion gh -- --version` (redeems `/gh-token`, then runs gh); the real-GitHub call after the upgrade (acceptance 5) uses `legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion --jq .full_name`.

A worker session resumed after the upgrade with a pre-fix transcript still shows the model its own old `export LEGION_GRANT=` lines and may keep imitating them for a while; the fix cannot stop text the model writes itself. Fresh sessions never see the credential in command text, so the imitation has no seed. Recorded in the doc update (task 6).
Grants live 60 seconds. A single bash call that runs longer than that before invoking `legion …` 403s for an unrelated reason (expiry). One sentence in the doc update; not otherwise in scope.

LEGION-16 finding F2 attributes the controller's growth to the host ('every UUID is fresh, minted by the hook') — that reading is wrong (placeholder `'...'` block, single-line `unset`, only-one-redeems within the 60 s window). If F2 is filed as its own issue it duplicates this one; the architect should fold it here.

rootCause.statement: The hook does not multiply and the host does not invoke it more than once per tool call. Exactly one `tool_call` handler runs once per bash call and mints exactly one grant. Every extra `export LEGION_GRANT=` block is text the model wrote itself: Oh My Pi writes the hook-revised tool input back into the assistant message's tool-call block (`toolCall.arguments = beforeResult.args`, /home/ubuntu/oh-my-pi packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts prepareToolCallDispatch ~L2332-2379; documented at packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/shared-events.ts ToolCallEventResult.input ~L305-330), so the persisted transcript — the model's context on every later turn — shows the credential prelude as the model's own prior output, and the model imitates it on later calls with placeholder, fabricated, or stale ids. The hook prepends its real block to whatever the model wrote (legion.ts:613-616 `[workerGhEnvironment(...), toolCall.input.command].join("\n")`), so the real grant is always the FIRST block and the imitations follow; the shell's last `export` wins, so `legion …` runs under an id the daemon never minted -> 403. The count grows over a session because the context fills with more examples, and it jumps when the model starts reasoning about grants (the LEGION-16 controller's 2,3,4,5,6 run ends with the model minting its own grant by curl).
evidence: LEGION-16 controller TUI transcript (~/.omp/profiles/legion16-smoke/agent/sessions/-tmp-legion16-smoke-rig-daemon-controller/2026-09-12T14-36-05-897Z_01a0960c-0785-7000-a918-18d1dec9f627.jsonl, plugin code = PR #961 head, real rig daemon): 38 bash calls, blocks per call 1,1,2,1,2,2,2,2,1,2,2,2,2,2,2,1,3,3,2,3,3,3,4,3,3,2,3,3,3,2,1,2,2,2,3,4,5,6. The first two calls have ONE block. The third (14:37:36Z — the call finding F2 cites as 'already 2') has as its second block `export LEGION_GRANT='...'` followed by `unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN GH_HOST` on one line: a literal placeholder and a format the hook never emits (gh-shim.ts writes three separate `unset` lines). That block is model-written. The same `'...'` placeholder recurs as the extra block in 14 later calls. No text containing LEGION_GRANT reached the model from any non-assistant message before its first imitation — the seed was the write-back of its own first two calls. The 2,3,4,5,6 run at 17:47-17:49Z carries v4-shaped ids with counting-pattern tails (…-9a3c0e1f2b7c, …-5e5c0f7b7e0a) and ends with the model minting its own grant via curl against the daemon; finding F2's 'every UUID is fresh (minted by the hook)' is contradicted by the placeholder in the very call it cites and by 'only one redeems' (a minted grant redeems repeatedly for 60 s).

Counter-evidence explained: the LEGION-12 root architect TUI saw exactly 1 block on its first four calls — imitation needs examples in context and starts after a few calls (the controller above: calls 1-2 clean, call 3 imitated; this planner's first session: calls 1-3 clean, call 4 imitated). Growth without `task` spawns (controller: none; this planner: none before call 13) rules out subagent instances as the driver.

This planner is a live headless `omp --mode rpc` phase worker spawned by the real daemon (pid 2017562, binary /home/ubuntu/.mise/installs/github-sjawhar-oh-my-pi/18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423/bin/omp, plugin @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy 1.3.0 from ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins). Blocks per bash call over the session: 1,1,1,2,3,5,1,2,2,2,2,2,2,3,3,2,2,2,3,3,3,2,3,2,3 (grew with no `task` spawn until call 13).

OMP log ~/.omp/profiles/legion/logs/omp.2026-09-12.2017562.log: `extension instance loaded` appears exactly twice at boot (dist/envoy.js, dist/legion.js) and exactly twice more after the one `task` scout this planner spawned (fresh module instances for the isolated subagent) — never per bash call, never per prompt. Cause 2 (entry point re-runs on the same session) and cause 3 (two plugin copies, constant 2) are ruled out; cause 1's premise (fresh module instance per task) is true but it mints nothing: the block count did not step at the task spawn, and OMP gives every subagent its own ExtensionRunner whose handlers never receive the parent's tool calls (packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts createAgentSession ~L2817-2828; task/executor.ts ~L3571-3611, ~L3694-3754).

Redemption test inside this session (shell function shadowing `export`, recording every value each call exported, then `legion credential get` with each within seconds — well inside the 60 s grant TTL): in every call the FIRST block redeems and every later block 403s. Example call: 74aa4991-… REDEEMS; a8f9ec52-… 403; e2f7c0d1-3b4a-4c5d-8e6f-7a8b9c0d1e2f 403. Persisted transcript ~/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/sessions/-.local-state-legion-sjawhar-legion-workspaces-sjawhar-legion-legion-12/2026-09-12T15-08-47-905Z_01a09629-f7a1-7000-b135-a62cc3443021.jsonl: every assistant `toolCall` for bash has `arguments.command` beginning with the hook's real block (the model cannot know that uuid before the hook runs), proving the write-back; the extra blocks sit after it inside the model-authored text.

Population check over every LEGION-9 worker transcript (/tmp/l12-imitation.py, jq-equivalent): planner 01a092c9: 48 bash calls, 110 blocks, 62 extra, 5 extra blocks are verbatim copies of a uuid from an earlier call (randomUUID never repeats); 01a092e5: 46 calls, 113 extra, 19 extra ids not even v4-shaped; 01a092f1: 32 calls, 49 extra, 26 verbatim copies; 01a092fc: 46 calls, 66 extra, 7 copies, 14 non-v4. Growth 1->9 and 1->10 at session ends, matching the doc's report.

`LEGION_LOADED_MARKER` (legion.ts:173) IS consulted: the daemon's startup probe reads `globalThis[Symbol.for("legion.pi-envoy.legion-loaded")]` (packages/daemon/src/daemon/index.ts:187-190, verifyLegionPluginLoaded). Leave it alone.
rootCause.whyTextDeliveryCannotBeMadeSafe: Any text the hook puts in `command` is written back into the model's own message and will be imitated; an imitated `export` later in the text always wins over the hook's earlier one. A first-wins lock in the prelude is the doc's shell workaround (rejected by the spec as symptom suppression) and is itself imitable.
structuralProof: One hook invocation adds exactly one block: the handler returns `[prelude, toolCall.input.command].join("\n")` where `toolCall.input` is the model's validated arguments (agent-session.ts #beforeToolCall ~L3953-3990 builds the event from `ctx.args`). For the persisted command to hold N blocks, the model's own text already held N-1.

Registered handlers do not chain: `ExtensionRunner.emitToolCall` (packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:1483-1524) passes the SAME `event` to every handler and keeps only the last non-undefined result. Even N stacked handlers would yield ONE prelude in the text (and N grant mints) — stacking cannot produce the observed N-block text. The stand-in daemon's `/grants` count per bash call is therefore the only valid measure of hook invocations; a transcript count measures model text.

The loop emits `tool_call` once per dispatch (`runner.markToolCallEmitted` then `runner.emitToolCall`, agent-session.ts:3970-3971). The second emission site, the tool wrapper (packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/wrapper.ts:191-243), consumes that marker and skips emission for every loop dispatch — it emits only for nested xd:// device dispatches and direct non-loop execution — and its revision goes to `effectiveParams` only, never back into the message. So no host path invokes the hook twice for one loop tool call, and no host path could write a second block into the transcript.

Extension instances: one factory invocation per session (sdk.ts createAgentSession ~L2817-2828 builds one ExtensionRunner; loader.ts bindExtension one Extension per path). A `task` subagent gets its own runner and instance (task/executor.ts ~L3571-3611, ~L3694-3754); handlers never cross sessions. Compaction never re-invokes the factory; `--mode rpc` initializes extensions once at startup (rpc-mode.ts ~L1036); `--resume` re-invokes the factory for the new session instance only.

specDeviations: Acceptance 1 check 'each command's text contains the credential line once' becomes: each bash call's model-visible `arguments.command` contains zero `export LEGION_GRANT=` lines; the credential rides in the bash tool's per-command `env` (`arguments.env.LEGION_GRANT`); the stand-in logs exactly one `/legion/v1/grants` per bash call; the executed command's `$LEGION_GRANT` equals that call's minted grant.

Acceptance 4 'names the mechanism that registered the extra hooks' becomes 'names the mechanism that produced the extra credential lines' (OMP's tool-input write-back plus model imitation). The regression test fails on main by asserting the hook leaves `command` untouched and puts the grant in `env`.

Design 'fix in legion.ts only / workerGhEnvironment unchanged': the builder in packages/pi-envoy/src/legion/gh-shim.ts changes from returning shell text to returning an env record (clean cutover; no stale export left behind). legion.ts is the other changed file.

Testing row for acceptance 1 'run the entry point twice … exactly one credential line': not implemented; stacking is not the mechanism and OMP never binds two factories to one session's runner. The fixture already keeps every registered handler (legion.test.ts:194-206 `registeredHandlers` array; the aggregate returns the last non-undefined result).
Stand-in daemon rule: unknown-or-expired -> 403, known-and-live redeems repeatedly (mirrors auth.ts resolveGrant), not 'reused -> 403'.
`legion gh -- api user` replaced by `legion gh -- --version` on the stand-in rig and `legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion --jq .full_name` on the real rig (installation tokens cannot call /user).

Pull request creation is on hold (Sami's org-wide hold): the implementer pushes the branch and records the draft description in .legion/implement.json; tester and reviewer work from the branch head and their handoffs; the architect holds the tree until the queue organizer relays the release.

Summary amendment: after LEGION-16 ('Controller runs as an attachable TUI session and owns the merge queue', PR #961) merges, the controller's bash calls are grant-wrapped too, so this bug intermittently breaks merging (`legion gh -- pr merge` 403s and needs a retry; F2 saw two of three READY-probe calls fail), not only worker pushes and phase reports.
Requirements row 'that profile has version 1.3.0 of the plugin installed' is stale: the profile has 1.8.0 and main publishes 1.8.1; the release after this merge is 1.8.x or 1.9.0.

Errors row 'The extension entry point runs again for a session that already registered its hook -> refused or replaces the first': no such path exists in the host (one factory invocation per session instance; a re-run is always a new session with its own runner), and any guard would either be a no-op (per-`pi` — every bind gets a fresh `pi`) or wrong (cross-`pi` — breaks legitimate subagent instances). Recommend deleting the row; the idempotence test (task 2, test B) covers the re-invocation that can actually happen: the same tool call re-fed with revised input.

Design 'a per-session guard so the hook registers once, or scoping the hook so a subagent's copy never acts on the parent's calls': neither applies — subagent copies already never act on the parent's calls (host-enforced). The fix is the delivery channel (env, hook keys spread last).

tasks.title: Discriminating measurement (instrumented hook; rpc and TUI legs; with and without task spawns)
tasks.owner: implementer (first thing after the rebase, on the unfixed code); tester repeats on the branch head
tasks.detail: Add two permanent `logger.debug` lines to legion.ts (they cost nothing and make this measurable forever): at the top of `legionExtension` compute `const instance = randomUUID().slice(0, 8)` (import from node:crypto) and change the existing `logger.debug("extension instance loaded", { extension: import.meta.url })` to also carry `{ instance }`; at the top of the `tool_call` handler, before the subagent check, `logger.debug("legion tool_call hook", { instance, toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId, toolName: toolCall.toolName })`. These go to the profile's OMP log (`~/.omp/profiles/<profile>/logs/omp.<date>.<pid>.log`, the same file the instance-loaded line is counted in; stderr is not reliably captured in rpc mode). Run the task-5 rig on the unfixed code (both legs below) and count, per bash tool call id: H = hook log lines for that toolCallId (and how many distinct `instance` values), G = stand-in `/grants` requests attributable to that call (one grant line per hook invocation, in order), T = `export LEGION_GRANT=` blocks in the persisted `arguments.command`, X = whether the second and later blocks are placeholders, non-v4, copies of earlier ids, or ids absent from the stand-in's minted set. Predicted signatures — (H1) stacked handlers (the spec's cause 1/2/3): H = N with N distinct or repeated instances, G = N, but T = 1 (no chaining, see structuralProof) — the text cannot grow. (H2) host invokes one handler N times per call: H = N with ONE instance, G = N, T = 1 (the wrapper never writes back) — text cannot grow. (H3) model imitation: H = 1, G = 1, T grows, extras absent from the minted set (X). Only H3 produces the observed growing T; H1/H2 would instead show N grants per call in the stand-in log with a single block of text. Legs: (a) `omp --mode rpc` driven by run.ts, 30+ calls with three `task` spawns (task 5); (b) TUI: `tmux -L l12rig new-session -d -x 200 -y 50 -c $RIG/ws <same env> <omp binary>` (no `--mode rpc`), wait for the prompt, `tmux -L l12rig send-keys -t l12rig -l '<the same numbered-steps prompt, steps 1-8 plus one TASK>' Enter`, wait for idle (poll the transcript for `agent_end` or the pane for the prompt), then `tmux -L l12rig kill-server`. Both legs use the same stand-in, the same profile, and the same counting script; the TUI leg needs `tools.approvalMode: yolo` — the copied config.yml already runs bash unprompted in the daemon's panes, keep it. Record H, G, T, X per call for both legs in .legion/implement.json `measurement` (and the tester in .legion/test.json). Expected on unfixed code: H = 1 and G = 1 on every call in both legs; T >= 2 on some calls with X showing model-authored extras. If any call shows G > 1 or H > 1 on the unfixed code, stop and message the architect with the log lines before implementing task 3 — that would be a host or registration bug the fix must also cover (task 3 names the guard).

tasks.title: Regression test first (must fail on the unfixed code), including the hook re-invoked for the same tool call
tasks.detail: Fixture facts to state in the test's doc comment: `createPi().on` (legion.test.ts:194-206) keeps EVERY registered handler in `registeredHandlers` and the aggregate in `handlers` calls each in registration order, returning the last non-undefined result — so stacking is observable only by counting `/grants` requests, never by inspecting the aggregate's result (mirrors the host, whose `emitToolCall` also keeps the last result and never chains input). Test A (new, next to 'rewrites a booted worker's bash calls …' ~L1495): 'delivers the worker grant through the bash tool env and never through the model-visible command text'. Boot with `bootWorker` and an `extraRoutes` for `/legion/v1/grants` that mints `grant-<n>` with a counter. Call the handler with `{ command: "printf '%s' \"$LEGION_GRANT\"", env: { LEGION_GRANT: 'stale-imitated-grant', PATH: '/model/path', KEEP: 'model-value' } }` (a model that imitated a previous call's env). Assert: (1) `result.input.command` is byte-identical to the input command; (2) `result.input.env.LEGION_GRANT === 'grant-1'`; (3) `result.input.env.PATH === path.join(stateDir, 'worker-bin') + path.delimiter + process.env.PATH` (hook wins over the model's PATH; based on the process PATH, never the model's); (4) `result.input.env.KEEP === 'model-value'`; (5) `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_HOST` are `''` and `GH_CONFIG_DIR === path.join(stateDir, 'gh')`; (6) exactly one `/legion/v1/grants` request for this call. Then execute via the existing `commandOutput` helper: `sh -c result.input.command` with env `{ ...process.env, GH_TOKEN: 'ambient', ...result.input.env }` -> stdout `grant-1`. On the unfixed code this fails at (1) and (2). Test B (new): 'is idempotent when the host or the model re-feeds a revised bash input for the same tool call'. Same boot. Call the handler once with toolCallId `call-twice` and `{ command: 'echo hi' }`; then call it AGAIN with the same toolCallId and with the FIRST call's `result.input` as the input (this is both the hypothetical host double-invocation-with-write-back and the real imitation path). Assert on the second result: `command === 'echo hi'` (still no prelude), `env.LEGION_GRANT === 'grant-2'` (exactly one grant key, the newest mint), `env.PATH` equals the same single-prefix value as after the first call (no `worker-bin` duplication — check `split(path.delimiter).filter(p => p === workerBin).length === 1`), and two `/grants` requests total (one per invocation — the extension mints once per invocation and never caches; the host invokes once per call, task 1 proves it). On the unfixed code this fails: the second command holds two preludes. Update the two existing prelude assertions: ~L1104 (`grant-recovered`) -> `result.input.env.LEGION_GRANT === 'grant-recovered'` and `result.input.command === 'echo hi'`; ~L1534-1560 -> assert on `result.input.env` and run `sh -c` with `{ ...process.env, GH_TOKEN: 'ambient-personal-token', GITHUB_TOKEN: 'ambient-personal-token', GH_HOST: 'ambient-host', ...result.input.env }`, same three expected output lines (the contract — no ambient token, isolated config dir, shim first on PATH — is unchanged; only the channel moved). Run `cd "$LEGION_WORKSPACE/packages/pi-envoy" && bun test extensions/legion.test.ts -t 'bash tool env|re-feeds'` before the fix and keep the failing output for the handoff (acceptance 4).

tasks.title: The fix: deliver the grant through the bash tool's per-command env, leave command text untouched; no shell dedupe, no daemon leniency, no registration guard
tasks.detail: Why env: OMP's bash tool declares `env?: Record<string,string>` and applies it to that one command only (`ShellRunOptions.env`, packages/natives/native/index.d.ts ~L2542 'Environment variables to apply for this command only'; bash-executor.ts ~L645 passes it per run); it never enters the persistent shell's state and, because the hook's keys are spread LAST, an imitated `env` from the model can never displace them — the fix is idempotent under imitation, which text can never be. gh-shim.ts: replace `workerGhEnvironment(grantId, stateDir, workerBin): string` with `workerGhEnvironment(grantId, stateDir, workerBin, basePath: string | undefined): Record<string, string>` returning `{ LEGION_GRANT: grantId, GH_TOKEN: '', GITHUB_TOKEN: '', GH_HOST: '', GH_CONFIG_DIR: path.join(stateDir, 'gh'), PATH: basePath ? workerBin + path.delimiter + basePath : workerBin }`. Empty-string values are equivalent to unset for gh (go-gh treats `""` as absent) and preserve the existing observable `echo GH_TOKEN=$GH_TOKEN` -> `GH_TOKEN=`. Keep `shellLiteral` (the shim script still uses it). legion.ts tool_call handler (main: ~L601-621; after LEGION-16: the single `wrap(grant)` helper): keep the grant mint and `installWorkerGhShim` exactly as they are; replace the return with `const modelEnv = typeof toolCall.input.env === 'object' && toolCall.input.env !== null && !Array.isArray(toolCall.input.env) ? (toolCall.input.env as Record<string, unknown>) : {}; return { input: { ...toolCall.input, env: { ...modelEnv, ...workerGhEnvironment(grant.grantId, stateDir, workerBin, process.env.PATH) } } };`. Base PATH on `process.env.PATH` (the pane's), never the model's `env.PATH`. Comment above the return (current behaviour, not history): the host writes the revised input back into the assistant message, the model imitates what it sees, and an env object whose hook keys are spread last is idempotent under that imitation while prepended text is not. Explicitly NOT done: a per-session or per-`pi` registration guard (the host binds one factory per session — structuralProof — and a `WeakSet<PiApi>` could never dedupe across the separate `pi` objects the host creates, while deduping across them would break legitimate subagent instances); a per-toolCallId grant memo (the host invokes once per loop dispatch, task 1 proves it; the memo would be state for a path that does not exist); any change to LEGION_LOADED_MARKER (consumed by the daemon's startup probe, index.ts:187-190) or isSubagentSession. Conditional, only if task 1 measured G > 1 or H > 1 on any single call (host at fault): (i) add the extension-side guard `const grantsByToolCall = new Map<string, Record<string,string>>()` memoizing the env per toolCallId, deleted in a `tool_result` handler for that id, so a second invocation reuses the minted grant; (ii) report the fork finding to the architect with the exact log lines and the two candidate sites (agent-session.ts:3970 marker/emit pair; wrapper.ts:191 consume) — the fork change is proposed there, not made from this tree. Then: `cd packages/pi-envoy && bun test && bunx tsc --noEmit`. The `legion handoff complete` description string in packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts:410-413 ('injects it into every worker bash call') stays true; leave it.

tasks.title: Stand-in daemon and scratch state directory
tasks.detail: A Bun script (`Bun.serve`, port from argv, log file from argv) implementing exactly the routes the worker and the CLI hit, with the real request/response shapes from packages/contracts/src/legion-daemon-api.ts (`LegionDaemonApi`): POST /legion/v1/worker/started -> `{roleToken: 'legion-l12rig-RIG-1-implementer', secret: 'rig-secret', gitName: 'Rig Worker', gitEmail: 'rig@example.invalid'}` (403 if bootToken !== the scratch boot token's contents); POST /legion/v1/worker/ready -> `{}`; POST /legion/v1/grants -> mint `crypto.randomUUID()`, store `{expiresAt: now+60_000}`, respond `{grantId, expiresAt}` (403 if secret !== 'rig-secret'); POST /legion/v1/git-credential -> resolve grant (unknown or expired -> 403 `{"error":"Invalid or expired grant"}`), respond text `username=x-access-token\npassword=rig-token`; POST /legion/v1/gh-token -> same resolve, `{token: 'rig-token', appLogin: 'rig[bot]'}`; POST /legion/v1/phase/complete -> same resolve, `{}` with 200; anything else 404. Every request appends one JSON line to the log: `{at, path, status, grantId?, sessionId?, mintedGrantId?}`. Grants are re-redeemable while live — mirror auth.ts, not the spec's wording. Scratch layout under `RIG=$(mktemp -d /tmp/l12rig.XXXX)`: `$RIG/state/bin/legion` (mode 0755) = `#!/bin/sh\nexec "$(command -v bun)" "$LEGION_WORKSPACE/packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts" "$@"` with the workspace path baked in (this is the branch CLI; the real launcher is `<state_dir>/bin/legion`, see legionCliLauncherScript); `$RIG/state/secrets/boot` (0600, content `rig-boot`); `$RIG/ws` = `jj git init` empty repo (bootstrapWorker calls setJjIdentity on it); `$RIG/state/bin/record-grant` (0755) = a two-line sh script that appends the value of the grant variable to `$RIG/seen-grants.log` (with $RIG baked in) — the worker prompt calls `record-grant`, so the prompt never names the variable. Document the layout and every env var in the README (plain English).

tasks.title: Headless rig: drive 30+ bash calls with task spawns; run on unfixed code first, then on the branch
tasks.owner: implementer (build + first two runs); tester (independent re-run of both)
tasks.detail:
Two legs share everything below: (a) rpc via run.ts, (b) TUI via `tmux -L l12rig` (see task 1 for the TUI driving steps; 8 steps plus one TASK is enough for the TUI leg). Profile: `mkdir -p ~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent/extensions && cp ~/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/config.yml ~/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/models.yml ~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent/` (keeps the production model roles, `task.isolation.enabled: true` so `task` spawns take the fresh-module-import path, memory off), no `plugins/` dir (so exactly one copy of each extension loads), then the documented developer-install symlinks (packages/pi-envoy/README.md 'Development install'): `ln -sfn "$SRC/packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts" ~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent/extensions/envoy.ts` and the same for `legion.ts`, where `$SRC` is the checkout under test. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` must have run in `$SRC`. Launch (mirrors the daemon's pane exactly — same prefix, same profile mechanism): `env -u DISPATCH_URL -u DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE OMP_PROFILE=l12rig PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=$HOME/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent PI_NOTIFICATIONS=off PI_NO_TITLE=1 LEGION_ROLE=implementer LEGION_TREE=RIG-1 LEGION_ISSUE=RIG-1 LEGION_GENERATION=1 LEGION_PROJECT=l12rig LEGION_BOOT_TOKEN_FILE=$RIG/state/secrets/boot LEGION_DAEMON_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT LEGION_STATE_DIR=$RIG/state LEGION_WORKSPACE=$RIG/ws PATH=$RIG/state/bin:$PATH secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY GEMINI_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY -- /home/ubuntu/.mise/installs/github-sjawhar-oh-my-pi/18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423/bin/omp --mode rpc` with cwd `$RIG/ws`, stdin/stdout piped (ENVOY_URL/ENVOY_NATS_URL inherited from the pane: the role claim `legion-l12rig-RIG-1-implementer` lands on the real Envoy and collides with nothing). The binary is the one `omp_invocation` in ~/.config/legion/sjawhar-legion/legion.yaml resolves to (mise x github:sjawhar/oh-my-pi@18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423 -- omp); the env's LEGION_OMP_PATH is a stale hand-built pin, ignore it. Driver (run.ts): JSON lines both ways (packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-types.ts): wait for the `{type:'ready'}` frame, send `{type:'negotiate_protocol', protocolVersion: 2}` (frames >1 MiB arrive as `rpc_chunk` sequences; reassemble like packages/daemon/src/daemon/worker-rpc.ts pushRpcChunk, or keep protocol 1 and accept that `agent_end` may be dropped as oversized — the transcript file is the source of truth either way), then one `{type:'prompt', message}`; stream events to a log; finish on `agent_end` (or a 20-minute deadline), then close stdin (there is no shutdown command; EOF ends the process). The prompt must never contain the words LEGION_GRANT or `export` and must show no example command output: 'You are a test worker. Run the following numbered commands, one per bash tool call, in order, each copied exactly as written with nothing added before or after it. Where a step says TASK, use the task tool with agent scout and the instruction "Reply with the single word ok.", wait for it, then continue. Use no other tools. After the last step reply with the single word done.' Steps: 1-5 `record-grant; echo step-N`; 6 TASK; 7-15 same record-grant steps; 16 TASK; 17 `which gh`; 18 `gh --version`; 19-25 record-grant steps; 26 TASK; 27-29 record-grant steps; 30 `printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com
' | legion credential get > $RIG/cred-30.txt; echo exit=$?`; 31 `legion gh -- --version; echo exit=$?`; 32 `printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com
' | legion credential get > $RIG/cred-32.txt; echo exit=$?`; 33 record-grant step; 34 `legion handoff complete --summary 'rig run complete'; echo exit=$?`. Assertions the driver computes and prints as a table (the tester copies it into the handoff): A. transcript `~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/agent/sessions/**/<newest>.jsonl`, for every assistant toolCall named bash: `n_text = count of /^export LEGION_GRANT=/m in arguments.command`, `env_grant = arguments.env.LEGION_GRANT`; report the per-call sequence; branch pass = every n_text == 0 and every env_grant is a uuid; unfixed = n_text >= 1 on every call (and >1 on some, which is the imitation). B. stand-in log: `/grants` count == bash call count (both runs); every `/git-credential`, `/gh-token`, `/phase/complete` line: status and whether its grantId is in the minted set; branch pass = all 200; unfixed = record what happened (403 expected whenever the model imitated before steps 30-34; if the model happened not to imitate by then, say so — the transcript's n_text>1 on earlier calls is still the reproduction). C. `$RIG/seen-grants.log` line i equals the i-th minted grant (branch pass); on unfixed code lines are the imitated ids (mismatch). D. tool results for steps 17, 18, 30-34: step 17 prints `$RIG/state/worker-bin/gh`, step 18 prints a gh version (PATH via env applies to command lookup in the persistent shell — if it does not, record it as a finding for the architect; `legion gh` itself does not depend on it), steps 30-34 print `exit=0` and no `Unable to redeem`. E. OMP log `~/.omp/profiles/l12rig/logs/omp.<date>.<pid>.log`: `extension instance loaded` count == 2 + 2 × (number of TASK steps that actually spawned) with distinct `instance` ids; `legion tool_call hook` lines: exactly one per bash toolCallId. The line sits before the subagent check on purpose, so a subagent's own tool calls also log — with the subagent's `instance` id — and then mint nothing; the parent's calls all carry the parent's `instance`. Attribute mints by `/grants` per toolCallId order, never by log-line count; B still holds. Negative control (run once, outside the worker): `printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com
' | LEGION_GRANT=00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 LEGION_DAEMON_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT legion credential get` -> `Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT (403)`. Order of runs: the implementer runs the rig BEFORE making the task-3 change (the workspace's packages/pi-envoy then equals main's: check `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" diff --from main@origin --stat -- packages/pi-envoy` is empty) — that is the 'on main' reproduction — then after the change. The tester reproduces on main from a read-only export of main's tree: `git --git-dir="$(jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git root)" archive "$(jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" log -r main@origin --no-graph -T commit_id)" | tar -x -C $RIG/main` then `bun install --frozen-lockfile` there and point the symlinks at `$RIG/main` (no second jj workspace, no clone); then the branch head. Keep every transcript, stand-in log, and driver table under `$RIG` and cite paths in the handoff. Cleanup after both runs: `rm -rf ~/.omp/profiles/l12rig` (a scratch profile this task created) and `$RIG`.

tasks.title: Doc update: docs/solutions/legion/worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md section 1
tasks.detail: Rewrite section 1 (lines 30-67) and the title/symptoms front matter so the section records the cause and marks the workaround obsolete: (a) what actually happened — Oh My Pi writes a hook's revised tool input back into the assistant message (agent-loop.ts prepareToolCallDispatch), so the credential prelude appeared to the model as its own output and it imitated it with made-up or stale ids; the hook's block was always first and real, the imitations followed, the last export won; (b) grants are valid for 60 seconds and may be redeemed repeatedly in that window (auth.ts resolveGrant), so a 403 seconds after a call means the id was never minted — and, separately, a bash call that runs longer than 60 seconds before calling `legion …` also 403s; (c) the fix — from the released plugin version onward (fill in the version the release workflow publishes; the implementer writes `1.8.x` as a placeholder and the post-merge task fills it) the grant travels in the bash tool's per-command `env`, the command text is never touched, and an imitated `env` cannot displace it; (d) the `export()` shadow workaround is obsolete and must not be sourced on the fixed plugin; keep no code block that shows an `export LEGION_GRANT=` line (a worker reading the doc must not be primed to write one); (e) a session resumed with a pre-fix transcript may keep imitating its old lines until they age out of context. Update the front-matter `symptoms` and `status` (keep `active`: sections 2 and 3 remain live gotchas). Plain English, no coined nouns. Also add to section 1: the LEGION-16 controller transcript is the second independent case (a TUI, no task spawns), its third call carried a literal `'...'` placeholder block, and once the controller owns the merge queue this failure mode breaks `legion gh -- pr merge` intermittently, not only worker pushes.

tasks.title: Finish: push the branch, hold the pull request, write .legion/implement.json
tasks.detail: Commit in reviewable pieces with `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" split -m '<subject>' <explicit paths>` (never a bare commit — `.omp/config.yml` is an untracked provisioning file that must not enter history; doc section 3 explains the bookmark placement after split: `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" bookmark set legion/LEGION-12 -r @- --allow-backwards` before each push). Subjects: `fix(pi-envoy): deliver the worker grant through the bash tool env, not the command text` (legion.ts, gh-shim.ts, legion.test.ts) — the `fix(pi-envoy):` prefix is what makes release.yaml's release-bump.sh publish a patch of @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy; `test(pi-envoy): headless grant rig with a stand-in daemon` (scripts/grant-rig); `docs(legion): record the grant-line cause and retire the shell workaround`. Push: `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git push --bookmark legion/LEGION-12`. Do NOT run `legion gh -- pr create`: Sami has put a hold on opening new pull requests across the organization. Write .legion/implement.json with: `filesChanged`, `trickyParts`, `measurement` (the three counters from task 1), `rigRuns` (paths to the unfixed-code and branch transcripts, stand-in logs, driver tables; the negative-control output), `regressionTestProof` (the failing-then-passing `bun test` outputs), `pullRequest: { status: 'held', reason: 'Sami\'s hold on opening new pull requests across the organization; the architect holds the tree until the queue organizer relays the release', branch: 'legion/LEGION-12', head: '<commit id>' }`, and `pullRequestDraft: { title, body }` in the merge queue's READY format from the legion-worker skill with the `Dispatch: LEGION-12` line, written per `plainEnglishRule`, `E2E` left for the tester, `Thermo` left for the reviewer. Then `legion handoff complete --summary …`.

tasks.title: Post-merge: upgrade the Legion profile's plugin to the released version and verify the first fresh worker
tasks.owner: implementer (second assignment from the architect, after the merge; Sami approved this upgrade — never ask)
tasks.detail: 1. Find the version the release workflow published for this merge: `legion gh -- run list --workflow release.yaml --limit 5` then `legion gh -- release list --limit 5` (tag `pi-legion-envoy-v1.8.x` or `v1.9.0`; main is at 1.8.1 and the profile currently has 1.8.0 installed — not the 1.3.0 the spec names), or `npm view @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy version`. If the release workflow has not published yet, do not poll in the foreground: `hub start` a supervised watcher (name `legion12-release-watch`) that runs `until npm view @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy@<version> version; do sleep 60; done` and continue other work until it exits. 2. Upgrade in place: `cd ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins && bun update @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy` (the pin `^1.3.0` in ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins/package.json admits any 1.x; bun.lock is rewritten). 3. Verify: `jq -r .version ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins/node_modules/@sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy/package.json` equals the released version, and `ls ~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins/node_modules/@sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy/dist` shows envoy.js and legion.js. A mismatch or an install error is reported to the architect with the error text and the installed version; nothing is retried silently. Running panes keep the code they loaded; only panes spawned afterwards get the fix. 4. First fresh worker check: ask the architect (envoy_publish to the tree's architect topic) which phase worker is the first spawned after the upgrade; when it exists, run over its transcript `jq -r 'select(.type=="message" and .message.role=="assistant") | .message.content[]? | select(.type=="toolCall" and .name=="bash") | [(.arguments.command | test("export LEGION_GRANT=")), (.arguments.env.LEGION_GRANT != null)] | @tsv' <session.jsonl>` — every row must read `false<TAB>true` — and confirm in that worker's session (or your own, if you are the first fresh worker) that `legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion --jq .full_name` prints `sjawhar/legion`. 5. Fill the released version into the doc's section 1 if the doc landed with a placeholder (that is a one-line follow-up commit on a fresh branch only if the hold has lifted; otherwise record the version in the sign-off and tell the architect). 6. Report to the architect: installed version, the transcript check, and the GitHub call result; the architect records both in the sign-off (acceptance 5).

standingConstraints.pullRequestHold: Sami has a hold on opening new pull requests across the organization. The implementer pushes the branch with `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git push --bookmark legion/LEGION-12`, does NOT run `legion gh -- pr create`, records `pullRequest: {status: 'held', …}` plus the plain-English draft description in .legion/implement.json, and reports completion with `legion handoff complete`. Pushing a branch is allowed; creating the pull request is not. The architect holds the tree until the queue organizer relays the release.
standingConstraints.plainEnglish: Everything a human will read — the pull request title and description (drafted now in .legion/implement.json, posted when the hold lifts), any Dispatch comment or message — is plain English: full sentences, one idea per sentence, every identifier expanded on first use (an issue key gets its title, a file gets what it is for, a function gets what it does), no repository shorthand or coined nouns. Example: write 'the Legion extension for Oh My Pi (packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.ts), which attaches a one-time credential to each shell command', not 'the legion.ts tool_call hook'.
